I’ll read the handoff and the existing E06 work, then continue the screen and record the findings and next steps in the investigation.

I’ve verified the formula inputs against the frozen packet and registered this chat in the investigation’s history. The screen will check the source and tail allowances first, then compare the prescribed midpoint panel count with the cap.

The source and tail bounds fit their budgets, but the prescribed panel count exceeds one million. The derivative term amplified by \(1/\delta\) dominates. The kernel term alone also exceeds the cap, which narrows what a successor method would need to change.

The result, replay script, and author check are filed. The progress register now marks E06 complete and leaves B05 proposed. The model-change note spells out the two methods B05 could compare and the costs each would need to account for.

**E06 r1 is complete. The prescribed uniform-midpoint recipe exceeds the one-million-panel cap.** At \(X=30,\ d=1/2,\ r=1\), the tail and source bounds fit their budgets. The 128-bit interval calculation placed the base-two logarithm of the required count before rounding between **5252.8622 and 5252.8623**, versus **19.9316** for the cap. The \(1/\delta\) derivative term dominates, and the kernel term alone also exceeds the cap at the selected cutoffs.

The result applies to this recipe’s sufficient allowance. Actual integration error, optimal cost, and the signed Green value remain undetermined. One reporting correction expanded the rejected-search entries to show their full intervals. It left the cutoffs and result unchanged.
